conclusion: No concrete regression found in the reviewed current call graph. The active, effective executor and exact workspace observation is limited to a validated Native read batch. Existing labelled background paths bypass it.

checks.topic: Real afterJob with inherited active scope
checks.result: after() captures all ALS via bindRequestCallback. afterJob enters runJob inside that restored callback; runJob then installs its own routeScope label. The existing v1 RED and v2 test run the actual afterJob while withReadBatchContext is still active, proving false/true fresh reads and unchanged foreground observation.

withReadBatchContext clears all policy maps and active=false in finally, including rejection. Promise<boolean> is the cache entry, so false is retained; the original read rejection is shared without conversion and a new batch reads again. Missing policy remains the existing true default.

The request pool proxy COMMIT_EXECUTOR resolves held client, request pool or default pool. Distinct actual executors and exact workspace strings separate entries; aliases of the same executor share only the same policy observation. The first read Promise is created in its original ALS scope. Ordinary/non-active readers return before accessing the executor metadata.

The original policy SELECT and params are unchanged. Own-key reads remain allowed when the shared policy is false; shared credential data, membership checks, connection states and exact credential grant SQL remain outside the memo. The Native closed action list still rejects mutating/nested actions before any invocation. No production writer or dispatch action was added to the batch.

currentRoute is innermost and withDatabaseOperation can overwrite a job label. In the reviewed current server call paths, these overrides occur in request/page/Server Action readers; no production afterJob/workflow path was found calling the policy-bearing coordinator action wrapper inside an inherited active batch. after:coordinator-wake uses wakeCoordinator -> coordinatorEnabled -> botModelReady -> resolveBotModelChoice -> usableApiKeys/pooled bindings without withDatabaseOperation. getModelOrder explicitly preserves currentRoute.

The added personal-policy -> read-batch-context edge reaches only existing revision/contract helpers plus the new commit-effects and labels imports. labels imports node:async_hooks only; commit-effects imports pg and node:async_hooks and has no back edge; live revisions/events and read-batch-contract have no personal-policy edge. No new static import cycle or import-time query was found.

nonblockingBoundary: This prefix check is not an immutable execution-kind capability. A constructed or future afterJob -> withDatabaseOperation(non-job label) -> policy read can hide the job label while the batch stays active. No such policy-bearing production call chain was established here, so this is recorded as a scope limitation rather than an invented production defect or new acceptance gate.
